messages.content: You are an expert programmer and mathematician.

Problem: A semi-circle of radius 8 cm, rocks back and forth along a line.  The distance between the line on which the semi-circle sits and the line above is 12 cm.  As it rocks without slipping, the semi-circle touches the line above at two points.  (When the semi-circle hits the line above, it immediately rocks back in the other direction.)  What is the distance between these two points, in millimetres, rounded off to the nearest whole number? [asy]

draw((-15, -8)--(15, -8));draw((-15, 4)--(15, 4));draw((-8, 0)--(8, 0){down}..{up}(-8, 0));

[/asy] (Note: After finding the exact value of the desired distance, you may find a calculator useful to round this value off to the nearest whole number.)

Solve step by step. End with: The answer is [your answer].

Previous draft (unverified):
Let the lower line be \(y=0\). The center of the semicircle is always \(8\) cm above this line.

The upper line is \(12\) cm above the lower line, so it is \(4\) cm above the center of the semicircle. When an endpoint of the semicircle touches the upper line, if the semicircle has rotated through angle \(\theta\),

\[
8\sin\theta=4
\]

so

\[
\sin\theta=\frac12 \implies \theta=\frac{\pi}{6}.
\]

While rolling without slipping, the center shifts horizontally by the arc length swept:

\[
8\theta=8\cdot \frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{4\pi}{3}\text{ cm}.
\]

At one extreme, the center shifts left by \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\), and the touching endpoint is \(8\cos\theta=4\sqrt3\) cm to the right of the center. Thus the contact point has coordinate

\[
-\frac{4\pi}{3}+4\sqrt3.
\]

The other contact point is its mirror image:

\[
\frac{4\pi}{3}-4\sqrt3.
\]

So the distance between the two contact points is

\[
2\left(4\sqrt3-\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)
=8\sqrt3-\frac{8\pi}{3}\text{ cm}.
\]

Converting to millimetres:

\[
10\left(8\sqrt3-\frac{8\pi}{3}\right)
\approx 54.788\text{ mm}.
\]

Rounded to the nearest whole number:

\[
\boxed{55}
\]

The answer is 55.
